section_1.title: Prerequisites: What is a Planar Graph?
section_1.content: Define a planar graph as a graph that can be drawn on a 2D plane without any edges crossing. Introduce the concept of 'Faces' (the enclosed regions including the infinite outer region).
section_1.example: Visualizing a 'Tetrahedron' graph: show it being flattened into a 2D shape where edges are pushed apart to avoid crossing.

section_2.title: The Core Concept: Euler's Characteristic Formula
section_2.content: Introduce the fundamental relationship: V - E + F = 2, where V = vertices, E = edges, and F = faces. Explain that this holds for all connected planar graphs.
section_2.example: An animation of a simple triangle (V=3, E=3, F=2) showing: 3 - 3 + 2 = 2.

section_3.title: Dual Graphs: The Concept of Reflection
section_3.content: Explain the dual graph construction: place a point in each face of the original graph and connect points if the faces share an edge. This shows how duals swap vertices and faces.
section_3.example: A 'Honeycomb' structure (the original graph) transforming into a 'Triangular Mesh' (its dual graph) as nodes connect across the center of each hexagon.

section_4.title: Practical Application: The Map Coloring Challenge
section_4.content: Demonstrate why Euler’s formula is critical for spatial constraints, such as the Four Color Theorem, using the dual graph concept to simplify map complexity.
section_4.example: Representing a map of a fictional island with 4 regions as a graph, then drawing its dual to find the most efficient way to place communication towers.

section_5.title: Summary and Synthesis
section_5.content: Recap the invariance of V - E + F = 2 and the reciprocal nature of dual graphs. Connect this back to the geometric intuition of why 'space' is restricted in planar networks.
section_5.example: A quick visual 'speed-run' showing a complex network collapsing into its dual and confirming the calculation remains true throughout the transformation.

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        lecture_texts = [Text("- " + line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
